title: הבטא של הסטארט-אפ

spec.palette: designed ramps, at most 5 steps each: plastic 4, amber 3, steel 3, board 2, glass 3, copper 2, red 1, ivory 2, mark 1

source: hand-placed pixels at 0 deg, every column (tools/art_host/weapons/beta_px.py); rows turned RotSprite-style (Scale2x x3, nearest), stray pixels out, a 1 px outline; the mark upright in the overlay only
character:
WHO: a start-up prototype blaster in a fat white 3D-printed shell: a REVOLVING DRUM of mismatched nozzles at the front
       (a copper hose barb, a steel funnel, an amber ring, a party horn, a toy propeller), an open panel with the bare
       green board glowing amber, a phone taped on as its screen, silver duct tape round the back, a coffee cup in a
       holder under the middle, a sticker with three logos. Nobody, the gun included, knows what the next pull does.
  IDLE: the phone shows loading dots; now and then an investor update pings (an envelope, the LED blinks) and a chart
        climbs. FIRE: it kicks, the screen flashes, then the drum SPINS like a roulette wheel while the phone loads, and
        clicks to a stop on a nozzle. CRASH: red sad face, sparks and smoke out of the board, the nozzle drum stuck
        half way; it goes black, boots (a power sign, a progress bar) and smiles as if nothing happened.
cell_note: a bigger cell than the contract's 64: it holds the weapon at every angle with its moving parts thrown out and the toss

equip.note: 18 ticks: it comes up from the hip with a black screen, the drum still; at 8 it BOOTS (the power sign, the LED), the progress bar runs, the loading dots: ready

idle.note: 2.6 s: the phone loads and loads (three dots, the bright one walks); an investor update pings (an envelope, the LED blinks twice), a chart climbs, back to loading

fire.note: 30 ticks = the cooldown. Tick 0 the shot: the screen flashes white, the whole gun kicks back and up; 2 the drum starts to turn; at 8 the SPINNER: the drum spins like a roulette wheel while the phone loads; it slows and clicks to a stop on the next nozzle (22-27), a settle

crash.note: 45 ticks, its RELOAD SHOW: the jam: the phone goes red with a sad face, sparks jump out of the board, the drum stuck half way; smoke puffs up, the drum sags a pixel, the screen dies; at 20 it REBOOTS: the power sign, a progress bar in three steps, and a smile as if nothing happened

empty.note: 12 ticks: the click on an empty battery (the icon, the red LED), a droop; at 6 he tosses it away in front of him, nose down, the tag trailing

catch.note: the hand-off from the unarmed catch (catch.json has the body's frames): it lands in his hands, boots, smiles; the reveal from the last frame

aim_note: a frame's aim = degrees the weapon turns from its rest (the idle's first frame is 0), added to the body's aim; kick = [px along the barrel (negative = back), px up, degrees up]
mark: the made-in-Israel mark as a SMALL HANGING TAG (the Host 12.11: the hull has no calm 13 x 13 place, so a tag at most 9 x 11 on a 3 px string): an ivory luggage tag with the blue outline star 7 x 7, on a blue-and-white cord from the swivel under the drum (behind the grip it covered the hero: the Host asked never to); upright and whole in every row, swinging by whole pixels with the kick, the spin and the toss. In atlas_mark.png ONLY (the Host's ruling)
mark_rect_note: per angle row, per column: [x, y, w, h] of the mark in the cell (the 9 x 11 tag, or the 11 x 11 roundel) and mark_star = the top-left pixel of the star (7 x 7 on the tag, 9 x 9 on a roundel); atlas_mark.png holds the mark alone in the same layout

events.draw: the gun comes up from the hip (arsenal.json equip 0)
events.boot: it boots (equip 8): the power sign, a start-up chime
events.ready: the act is over on this frame's last tick: can fire
events.anticipation: the 1-tick squash, on the shot's own tick (fire 0)
events.shot: the shot (fire 0): FX and the result on this frame, at `muzzle`
events.spinner: the drum spins, the phone loads (fire 8): the roulette rattle, then the click
events.jam: the crash (crash 0): the error buzz, sparks
events.reboot: the reboot (crash 20): the start-up chime again
events.click: the trigger on an empty battery (empty 0)
events.toss: the spent gun leaves his hand (empty 6)
events.reveal: RENDER fires the reveal from this pose

normal_note: by plane: every colour paints one plane of the weapon (top, front, underside ...), turned with the row; silhouette pixels face out along the edge; the upright mark faces the viewer

cells: the lid flat on the floor
sprites.anchor: the cell's TOP-left at `at` (frame px; the sprite stands on the cell's bottom, centred)

catch.note: the weapon's side of the unarmed set's catch, on the same ticks and hand points as the shotgun's catch.json (the body is one builder's): frames 0-2 it comes down, 3 the catch (its grip lands on the hand), 3-4 what carried it lets go, 5-6 in the hands, 7-9 held up behind his head (layer back), the reveal from 9. Its carrier is the box lid: on the catch it folds, then lies on the floor.

holds.note: THE SET'S OWN CARRY per hero body pose (the Host 12.11: a hero's face is never covered by his weapon in any pose). While the king plays one of these body animations with this weapon, draw the weapon at `aim` (degrees, the body's hand aim replaced) and its hand point moved by `offset` [x, y] px; the frame's own aim delta and kick still add. His port carry (aim 25-40) puts a long weapon across his chin and mouth; a low hip carry at -20 keeps the face and the crown clear (picture: art/weapons/host/previews/king_carry_long_weapons.png).
